newsitem.title: FRANCE: Essilor offers non-voting share conversion.
newsitem.headline: Essilor offers non-voting share conversion.

text.p: Contact lens manufacturer Essilor said on Wednesday that it was offering to convert preferred non-voting shares into common shares on the basis of one common share for one non-voting share plus 125 francs in cash.
"If all holders of preferred non-voting shares tender their shares for conversion, shareholders' equity will be increased by around 200 million francs," it said in a statement.
"The offer implicitly values the preferred non-voting share at 1,532 francs," based on the 1,657 franc closing price of the common share on Tuesday, it said.

"This represents an 11.6 percent premium to the last quoted price of the non-voting preferred share and around a 40 percent premium to the average price for the last six months," it said. The 1.63 million non-voting shares were trading at 1,373 francs on Tuesday.
Essilor said Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, which holds 22 percent of the preferred non-voting shares, plans to tender all of its shares to the offer.
Saint-Gobain already has a 21 percent stake in the lens maker and owns around a quarter of Valoptec, another company which holds a 17.4 percent stake in Essilor.
Officials at Saint-Gobain and Essilor were unavailable for comment.
Essilor said in its statement that the new common shares would carry rights to the 1996 dividend.
"In exchange for the loss of the preferred dividends, holders of preferred non-voting shares will gain the right to vote at shareholders' meetings," it said.
The transaction will be carried out through a simplified public exchange offer.

The move, approved unanimously on Wednesday by Essilor's board, has two objectives -- to boost equity and to offer holders of non-voting shares access to the common share market with its greater liquidity, Essilor said.
"The exchange will have a slightly anti-dilutive effect on earnings per share," it said.
An extraordinary shareholders meeting and special meetings of holders of preferred non-voting shares and convertible bonds will be held on March 3, it said.
Essilor shares, which were suspended on Wednesday, are scheduled to resume trading on the Paris bourse on Thursday morning. (( -- Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452))
